title: Plot Twist newsletter: Winston Churchill and the power of hobbies

vocab.articleQuote: the biggest retrospective of his art since 1958
vocab.meaning: A retrospective is a show that looks back over an artist's whole career, gathering work from many years in one place. The word starts with "retro," which means backward. In the article, a London museum is showing more than 50 of Winston Churchill's paintings from across his life.
examples: The museum held a retrospective of the cartoonist's work, from her first sketches to her latest comics.
After the band's last concert, the school put on a retrospective of its photos from ten years of shows.

vocab.articleQuote: Time has made some of the images feel more poignant
vocab.meaning: Something poignant makes you feel a gentle, deep sadness mixed with tenderness. It touches your heart. In the article, a painting of a happy family at the beach feels poignant now, because we know a big war was about to begin.
examples: Finding my old baby blanket in the attic was a poignant moment, because I remembered how small I used to be.
The last day of school felt poignant, since we knew we would not all be in the same class again.

vocab.meaning: Audacity is the boldness to try something even when it might not go well. Sometimes it also means daring to do something others think is too much. In the article, Churchill says you do not need special talent to paint, only the nerve to start.
examples: It took audacity for Sam to try out for the lead role when he had never acted before.
She had the audacity to ask the chess champion for a game, and she almost won.

concepts.name: Prime minister
concepts.articleQuote: Britain’s then prime minister, Winston Churchill
concepts.meaning:
Who is in charge of a country like Britain? Many countries have a **prime minister**, the leader who runs the government day to day. Britain also has a king or queen, but the monarch mostly handles ceremonies. The prime minister makes the big decisions about laws, money, and war.

Think of a school. The principal's name is on the door, but the person who actually decides the daily schedule and rules might be someone else. In Britain, the monarch is a bit like the name on the door, and the prime minister is the one making the schedule.

In the United States, the president does this job. A prime minister is different: they are usually the leader of the party that wins the most seats in the lawmaking group called Parliament, instead of being voted for directly by everyone.

So the takeaway: a prime minister is the head of the government in countries like Britain, and Churchill held that job during the second world war.

concepts.name: Biological age
concepts.meaning:
Can two people who are both 40 be different ages? Yes! Your **calendar age** is how many birthdays you have had. Your **biological age** is how old your body is acting, based on things doctors can measure, like how well your heart and cells are working.

Imagine two cars built the same year. One was driven hard and never fixed. The other was gently used and cared for. They have the same birthday, but one looks and runs much older.

The article says people who did something artistic once a week, like visiting a museum, were about a year younger biologically than people who rarely did. Their birthdays were the same, but their bodies seemed to be aging a little more slowly.

So the takeaway: biological age measures how old your body acts, and healthy habits can make it lower than your calendar age.

quiz.question: Why did Churchill start painting in 1915?
options: A teacher told him he had great talent
To distract himself after a professional downfall
He wanted to earn a living as a painter
He was asked to by the king
quiz.explanation: He began at age 40 to take his mind off the failed Gallipoli campaign.

quiz.question: What does Churchill say you need most to paint as a hobby?
options: Years of lessons
Expensive supplies
A natural gift for art
Audacity, or boldness
quiz.explanation: He said you do not need an innate gift, just sheer audacity.

quiz.question: According to Churchill, how many hobbies should a person have to be really happy and safe?
options: Exactly one
At least two or three
At least ten
None, because hobbies waste time
quiz.explanation: He argued that one ought to have at least two or three hobbies, and they must all be real.

quiz.question: What did the University College London study find?
options: People who did art or cultural visits weekly were about a year younger biologically
Painting makes people live ten years longer
Museums make people feel more stressed
Only experts get health benefits from art
quiz.explanation: Those who took part in an artistic pursuit once a week were about a year younger biologically.

quiz.question: What is a "retrospective" exhibit?
options: A show of only brand-new artwork
A show that looks back over an artist's career
A show where visitors paint too
A show that travels to many countries
quiz.explanation: A retrospective gathers work from across an artist's life, like the Churchill show in London.
